samples.summary: Non-owner test only counts "Remove member" buttons; it never checks the button is in the viewer's OWN row, so an inverted/wrong self-check still passes
samples.evidence: The new condition under test is `member.role !== "owner" && (isOwner || member.user.id === me?.id)` (workspace-settings.tsx:325-326). The test renders as MEMBER (id 2) with two non-owner members (ids 2 and 3) and asserts only `expect(screen.getAllByLabelText("Remove member")).toHaveLength(1)`. If the predicate were wrong in the opposite direction (e.g. `member.user.id !== me?.id`, rendering the trash button on OTHER_MEMBER's row instead of the viewer's), the count would still be exactly 1 and the test would stay green — i.e. the assertion is true regardless of which member the button belongs to. Asserting via the row (e.g. `within(screen.getByText("member").closest("tr"))`) is what would actually pin the behavior. Note the fixture has three members precisely to distinguish these cases, and the distinguishing assertion is the one that is missing.

samples.summary: Self-removal path is only asserted as rendered, never as functional: no test clicks the trash button or asserts removeMember is called with the viewer's own id
samples.evidence: The change deliberately keeps a remove button for the viewer's own row (comment at test lines 116-117 claims "self-removal is permitted by the backend"), but no test fires a click or asserts `removeMember` was called with (workspaceId, me.id). `removeMember` is mocked (test line 24) and never asserted on. I searched the whole test file and globbed packages/frontend/src/app/workspaces/** and src for other workspace-settings tests; this is the only one.

samples.summary: No coverage that a non-owner is denied the API Keys and Danger Zone sections, though the same `isOwner` value (whose computation this diff relocated) gates them and the api-keys query
samples.evidence: `isOwner` now also gates `fetchApiKeys`'s `enabled` (line 146) and both the API Keys (line 425) and Danger Zone (line 500) sections. The new test only asserts absence of "Create Invite"/"Invites"/"Revoke invite" for a non-owner (test lines 119-121); it never asserts "API Keys", "Create API Key", "Danger Zone" or "Delete this workspace" are hidden, nor that fetchApiKeys was not called — even though fetchApiKeys is mocked in the same block.

samples.summary: Negative assertions are anchored on the "Members" heading, which renders independently of the `me` query, so they can be satisfied by an unresolved auth state rather than by the owner gate
samples.evidence: `await waitFor(() => expect(screen.getByText("Members")).toBeTruthy())` waits only on the workspace query; the Members section (workspace-settings.tsx:299) renders as soon as `workspace` resolves, regardless of `me`. Before `fetchMe` resolves, `isOwner` is undefined, so "Create Invite"/"Invites"/"Revoke invite" are absent and `fetchInvites` uncalled for a reason unrelated to the gate. The following `toHaveLength(1)` happens to require `me` to be loaded, which rescues the ordering today, but it also makes the test order-dependent/flaky (if `me` resolves late the whole test fails). Anchoring on a `me`-dependent element inside waitFor would make the intent robust.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as written. workspace-settings.tsx:325-326 renders the "Remove member" button under `member.role !== "owner" && (isOwner || member.user.id === me?.id)`, inside the per-member TableRow (line 316). The fixture (test lines 30-55) has OWNER id 1, MEMBER id 2, OTHER_MEMBER id 3 (two non-owners). The non-owner test (lines 112-123) renders as MEMBER (id 2) and its comment claims "Only the viewer's own row keeps a trash icon", yet the only assertion for that behavior is a global count `expect(screen.getAllByLabelText("Remove member")).toHaveLength(1)` (line 118). Inverting the self-check to `member.user.id !== me?.id` would render the single button on OTHER_MEMBER's row instead, still yielding a count of exactly 1 and leaving the test green — so the assertion is true regardless of which member the button belongs to. A grep for "Remove member" across the repo shows only lines 104 and 118 of this test plus the component aria-label, so no row-scoped assertion (within/closest("tr")/username text) exists elsewhere. This is in-lane for test-adequacy (assertion that holds whether or not the feature works / missing distinguishing coverage for a changed behavior), and no guard or scope argument makes it moot.
